newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's wife says he optimistic about heart op.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's wife says he optimistic about heart op.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has "optimism in his eyes" about his forthcoming heart operation and is cracking jokes with his doctors, his wife Naina said in a television interview on Saturday.

Speaking to ORT television at the Barvikha sanatorium where Yeltsin is preparing for a bypass operation, she said the rest of the family were more nervous than Yeltsin himself. "Of course he is worried, but he is outwardly calm."
"He has a good contact with his doctors. I hear humour and jokes," she said, adding that Yeltsin was receiving lots of letters of support and many people were suggesting folk remedies.
"He has optimism in his eyes. As always when he has decided something he believes it will turn out all right," she added.

But she said the family were keeping from him news reports "which we think he should not see". She gave as an example newspaper attacks on his daughter Tatyana accusing her of bringing documents for her father to sign.
"That has never happened," she said. "People who write that have no idea how the civil service works."
Naina Yeltsin herself underwent a kidney operation in August. She looked in good health but acknowledged the family was in sombre mood.
No date has been set for Yeltsin's operation but officials say a decision by doctors could be imminent.
